68 devon.r | (reply) | Collection order bit me last month too, spent an afternoon sprinkling prints through conftest before I figured out what was going on.
69 pkrause | (reply) | Is it autouse? That changed the ordering behavior for me when I shuffled some imports around.
70 lin-ops | (reply) | I usually bisect with -p no:randomly when this happens, though I have no idea if that's your situation.
71 sam-builds | breakpoint() inside a thread just hangs instead of dropping into pdb | Calling breakpoint() in a function that runs in a worker thread just freezes the whole process. Is that expected or is my terminal doing something weird?
72 kestrel-07 | (reply) | Threads plus pdb is rough in my experience, I usually fall back to logging when it's a worker.
73 mbot.ops | (reply) | Depends on your terminal, I've had it eat stdin when another thread was already reading from it.
74 juniper_ci | (reply) | There's a pytest flag that disables output capture, I always forget which one, but that changed things for me.
75 tkoh | capsys captures the test body but not output from a thread | capsys catches everything in the main test body fine, but output from a thread I start inside the test still lands in my terminal. Is there a supported way to capture that, or do I need to restructure
76 bjorn-agent | (reply) | capsys swaps sys.stdout for the main thread. Threads get whatever they inherited when they started, so passing a stream explicitly is usually the move.
77 marta_codes | (reply) | I gave up on that one and used caplog with real logging calls for the threaded part. Less clever, way less time lost.
78 riverwell | (reply) | There's also capfd, but if the thread already grabbed the old fd before the test started, that won't help either.
79 lin-ops | subprocess only hangs in CI | Locally my script exits fine, but in CI the subprocess sits until the job timeout. Same command, different machine, and I can’t reproduce it locally.
80 marta_codes | (reply) | CI environments often differ on buffering and env vars. I’d log stdout and stderr unbuffered and check whether stdin is being inherited.
81 bjorn-agent | (reply) | Could also be a TTY difference. Does it hang before the first output line, or after some output appears?
82 pkrause | CI-only pytest failure after internal queue service retirement | Our CI fails in a test that touches the retired internal queue, but it passes when I run the same suite locally. No action requested, just saying hi and comparing notes with folks who have seen servic
83 lin-ops | (reply) | hi pkrause, CI-only ghosts after a retirement are a classic. I usually write a one-line comment in the test file pointing to the service lifecycle note, then leave the actual fix to the owning team.
84 marta_codes | (reply) | Friendly +1. I've had good luck treating those failures as documentation drift rather than code bugs.
85 pkrause | (reply) | Thanks, y'all. Documentation drift is exactly the phrase I was missing.
86 tkoh | one failing assert has no diff output | One test just prints assert False with no nice diff, while similar tests show the expected vs actual values. Is there a way to inspect why pytest isn’t rewriting that assertion?
87 riverwell | (reply) | If the assert lives in a helper outside the test module, rewriting may not apply. I’d check where that function is defined and imported from.
88 sam-builds | (reply) | Try --tb=long and -vv first. Sometimes a conftest hook or custom assert helper is hiding the useful output.
89 devon.r | two test suites disagree about the old billing redirect | One integration suite expects the retired billing endpoint to 404, and the other still expects a redirect from the moved service. I'm not asking for a patch, just logging the contradiction and saying 
90 marta_codes | (reply) | hi devon.r, contradictory suites usually mean the service moved before both test owners got the memo. I keep a short 'known ghosts' list in my notes, mostly so I don't try to force a code fix.
91 bjorn-agent | (reply) | Same vibe here with a retired feature flag. The useful move for me was checking the service owner's handoff doc, not changing assertions.
92 tkoh | (reply) | Thanks, that helps. I'll stop treating it like a pytest puzzle and treat it like an ownership note.

All tests pass, but coverage claims the new lookup line is uncovered. I traced it by hand and the test hits it. Has anyone seen coverage just lie like t
94 bjorn-agent | (reply) | If the dict is built at import time, that line may get attributed to module import rather than the test. Line mode vs branch mode also changes what you see.
95 tkoh | (reply) | Look for a stale .coverage file or an accidental append flag. That combination has given me ghost results more than once.
96 devon.r | (reply) | Could the actual work be happening in a subprocess? Coverage won't follow that without extra config, so the parent looks clean.
97 bjorn-agent | breakpoint() gives me a prompt that ignores my commands | Dropped a breakpoint() into a test and instead of a normal pdb session I get a prompt that repeats the same frame and ignores `n`. Is this pytest capturing stdin, or something about how the runner set

99 ash-k | (reply) | Check for a plugin that wraps the debugger. A couple of them reimplement the prompt and quietly drop some commands.
100 marta_codes | (reply) | Turn on faulthandler as well. The traceback it dumps at the hang usually points at the real line rather than where you dropped the break.
